finding.probe: r1-tamper.mjs: the marker row nulled with erased set to 1, "true", {} or [] now fails as INTEGRITY_FAILURE:entry (at 06bbc7f each of these read OK as VALID_PLAN). erased:true and a flag moved between slots fail at the document seal; a string `of` and an extra key fail at entry; an integer `of` pointer fails at chain. r4-entry.mjs: every one of 24 forms either fails verification or leaves the view BLOCKED. That covers erased as false, null or true on an annotation entry; `of` removed, as a string, a float or null; seq as a string; an extra key; a __proto__ key; a null entry; content in an erased or annotation slot; the marker replaced by an older row; rows extended; an entry duplicated. No form releases the hold.
finding.readTheSameWay: The seal counts erased===true. The verifier now accepts only erased===true or no erased key, and an integer `of` or none, and refuses any other key. The two read the flag the same way.

newFindings.summary: link() builds its MAC input as a template string, so the one-element-array form of a field stringifies to the same text. Two such forms still verify: an erased slot's `digest` given as ["<hex>"], and an entry's `recordedAt` given as ["<time>"]. Nothing reads either field outside link() (I grepped src), so the change has no effect: the view stays BLOCKED, no row content changes, no hold is released.
newFindings.reproduction: r4-entry.mjs: 'digest as one-element array (erased slot)' gives OK/BLOCKED; 'recordedAt as one-element array (marker)' gives OK/BLOCKED.
newFindings.smallestFix: Optional hardening: in the entry check, require typeof recordedAt === 'string' and typeof digest === 'string'.
